heading: INT. GLASSHOUSE CAFE - ORCHID CONSERVATORY - LATE AFTERNOON

units.text: INT. GLASSHOUSE CAFE - ORCHID CONSERVATORY - LATE AFTERNOON
Mist pools under the glass roof.
Hanging orchids drip.
A small iron table sits between a fig tree and a fogged window, laid for tea that has long gone cold.
WREN ACHTERBERG, thirties, a botanist with ink on her fingers, sits with her coat still buttoned, as though she means to leave.
Across from her, ANSELM DUPREE, late thirties, his tie loosened, turns a teaspoon over and over, as if it might yield an answer.
Behind them, the staff: MRS. OKAFOR, sixties, upright, in a green apron, polishes the same cup she has been polishing for a minute.
BAO, twenty, a waiter with an unsure grip on a tray, hovers near the fig tree and pretends to adjust a label.
I brought the seeds back.
units.name: ANSELM

units.text: I know. You said in your letter.
units.name: WREN

units.text: Four hundred of them. From the Andes.
units.name: ANSELM

units.text: That's a lot of seeds.
units.name: WREN

units.text: It's a lot of months.
units.name: ANSELM

units.text: She looks at the spoon in his fingers.
He sets it down.
I should have written more.
units.name: ANSELM

units.text: You wrote enough.
units.name: WREN

units.text: Wren.
units.name: ANSELM

units.text: I'm tired, Anselm. I've spent two years learning to be fine.
units.name: WREN

units.text: Mrs. Okafor sets down the cup.
Bao shifts the tray from one hand to the other.
More hot water.
units.name: MRS. OKAFOR

units.text: They haven't touched the first.
units.name: BAO

units.text: Then more hot water, Bao.
units.name: MRS. OKAFOR

units.text: Bao nods and flees toward the kitchen.
A door swings open on the far side of the conservatory.
A girl of nine steps in, ROSALIND, her coat buttoned wrong, a muddy satchel against her hip.
She stands under the dripping orchids and looks only at Anselm.
Papa?
units.name: ROSALIND

units.text: Wren's hand goes still on the table.
Anselm rises, the chair scraping the tile.
Rosalind. You were meant to wait with Aunt Hester.
units.name: ANSELM

units.text: She fell asleep. I came by myself. I know the way.
units.name: ROSALIND

units.text: Wren looks at the child.
At the buttons.
At Anselm.
Something in her face eases and breaks at once.
You didn't say you had a daughter.
units.name: WREN

units.text: I was afraid to.
units.name: ANSELM

units.text: Rosalind crosses to the table and studies Wren with grave attention.
Are you the lady with the plants?
units.name: ROSALIND

units.text: I suppose I am.
units.name: WREN

units.text: Papa said you know all their names.
units.name: ROSALIND

units.text: Wren reaches out and, slowly, fixes the girl's top button.
Her fingers are not quite steady.
Not all. But I could teach you some.
units.name: WREN

units.text: Mrs. Okafor, from across the room, sets the cup down at last and folds her cloth.
Bao returns with a copper pot, sees the table, and stops where he is, and does not speak.
